text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from massive amounts of text, such as books, websites, and articles. This training data helps them answer questions, write essays, or translate languages. To get good results, users often practice prompt engineering — writing clear and specific instructions. However, LLMs have limits. They can make mistakes, produce false information, or reflect biases found in their training data. They also cannot truly understand meaning like humans do. Despite these limits, LLMs are powerful tools for many language tasks.
